subject: RapidRetail production: post-incident governance delivery & follow-through
messages:
From: Anya Petrov <anya@rapidretail.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: RapidRetail SRE <sre@rapidretail.com>, Ben Cho <ben.cho@rapidretail.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: production errors + latency spike — need immediate readout

Hi Stephanie,

We're seeing a sustained latency spike and a concurrent increase in 5xx error rate across our inference routes (primarily the /generate and /chat endpoints) starting ~02:00 UTC yesterday. TPS is up ~2.8x for short bursts but the error rate increase looks tied to KV cache invalidations and autoscaling gaps. Our customers are reporting timeouts and degraded UX.

Can we get an executive readout and the RCA delivery timeline today? We need assurance on:
- Immediate mitigations and expected ETA to reach normal error rate
- Ownership for permanent fixes and expected SLAs
- Whether you’ll enable any temporary routing/fallback to a smaller model or region-level routing while you remediate

Attaching a short packet from our side with sampled traces and error logs (see attachment stub).

Thanks — this is high priority for us.

— Anya
Anya Petrov
Head of Platform Reliability, RapidRetail
anya@rapidretail.com

Attachments: rapidretail_incident_traces_1008.zip (attachment stub)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Anya Petrov <anya@rapidretail.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com, RapidRetail SRE <sre@rapidretail.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: production errors + latency spike — need immediate readout

Anya — thanks for flagging and for the traces.

We're on it. Immediate actions we've kicked off:
1) Canary routing configuration updated to direct 20% of RapidRetail traffic to the 2nd region to reduce single-region pressure (temporary).
2) Increased min-pool sizing for the fleet serving short-seq workloads to reduce cold-starts during burst periods.
3) Ops runbook activated: on-call SREs are streaming the KV cache metrics and retry ladder.

I'll lead an exec readout at 12:30 PM PT (today) to review the incident timeline, RCA hypothesis, and owner commitments. Deliverables we will produce by EOD: draft RCA PDF, mitigation runbook (short-term), and action owner matrix. Karthik will own the performance fix proposals; Jordan will coordinate customer-facing SLAs/credits if needed.

Can you confirm whether RapidRetail prefers a DocuSign for any SLA addendum or a quick email ack?

— Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com

Attachment: none

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Anya Petrov <anya@rapidretail.com>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com, RapidRetail SRE <sre@rapidretail.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Oct 2026 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: production errors + latency spike — need immediate readout

Thanks — adding more technical detail ahead of the exec call.

Preliminary findings (rapid triage):
- Root trigger: aggressive autoscaler cooldown combined with a model KV cache invalidation storm triggered by imbalanced request prefixes. When the cache misses spiked, backend tokenization/attention paths experienced higher memory pressure, causing OOM backoffs and increased 5xx responses.
- Contributing: a recent schedule change reduced reserved capacity for short-seq pools by 15% (rolled last week). That left less headroom for sudden TPS bursts.

Immediate corrective steps already in progress:
- Hotfix: revert reserve reduction for short-seq pool (in progress, ETA 18 minutes).
- Safety change: raise autoscaler minNodes by +2 for RapidRetail flittable pools for 48 hours.
- Fallback routing: enable model-compact variant (quantized v2) for requests exceeding 2s latency threshold.

Proposed post-incident actions and owners:
- A1: Permanent autoscaler policy adjustments and safety bounds (owner: karthik_iyer, ETA: 2026-10-13)
- A2: KV cache resiliency (prefix mitigation + early eviction heuristics) (owner: platform-infra-team / Jordan to coordinate cross-team, ETA: 2026-10-20)
- A3: Customer-facing SLAs & any one-off credit (owner: jordan_blake, ETA: 2026-10-11)
- A4: Regression test (load shape + prefix variance) to add to CI for future model onboards (owner: karthik_iyer, ETA: 2026-10-18)

I uploaded a draft RCA and mitigation runbook to the shared doc (link in thread). Will present the timeline and evidence in the 12:30 readout.

— Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Attachments: rapidretail_rca_draft_v1.pdf (draft), mitigation_runbook.xlsx (stub)

From: Anya Petrov <anya@rapidretail.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com, Ben Cho <ben.cho@rapidretail.com>, RapidRetail SRE <sre@rapidretail.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Oct 2026 12:52:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: production errors + latency spike — need immediate readout

Thanks, team — that helps.

We confirmed a 37% reduction in successful request rate during the window and have customer tickets piling up. The temporary routing you enabled helped most users within the hour but we want explicit SLAs and a written P0 mitigation timeline.

For the readout: please be prepared to share
- a short timeline of the failure (start, spike, mitigations applied and their immediate effect)
- the proposed owners and dates you listed above
- whether you will proactively route certain client keys to the compact model until full fixes land

DocuSign won't be needed today — a clear email acknowledgement is fine for the SLA addendum.

Looking forward to the 12:30 PT call.

— Anya

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Anya Petrov <anya@rapidretail.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com, RapidRetail SRE <sre@rapidretail.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 18:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: production errors + latency spike — need immediate readout

Anya — follow-up after today's readout. Thread summary and commitments below (finalized during the exec call):

Incident summary:
- Window: 2026-10-07T02:03:00Z — 2026-10-07T05:50:00Z
- Primary impact: elevated 5xxs and P95 latency on /generate and /chat for RapidRetail; peak TPS +2.8x versus baseline.
- Immediate effect of mitigations: Canary region routing + pool size increase reduced error rate from ~6.2% to ~1.1% within 45 minutes. Fallback to compact model cut tail latency by ~38% for affected requests.

Agreed corrective actions (owners & target dates):
- A1 (autoscaler policy safe-guards) — owner: karthik_iyer — target: 2026-10-13
- A2 (KV cache eviction heuristics & prefix mitigation) — owner: Platform Infra (Jordan to coordinate) — target: 2026-10-20
- A3 (customer SLA addendum & credit proposal) — owner: jordan_blake — target: 2026-10-11
- A4 (CI regression: load shape + prefix variance) — owner: karthik_iyer — target: 2026-10-18
- A5 (post-deployment verification + long-tail monitoring) — owner: platform-observability — target: 2026-10-21

Deliverables committed:
- Draft RCA (attached): rapidretail_rca_draft_v1.pdf
- Short-term runbook: mitigation_runbook.xlsx
- Exec readout recording: https://company.zoom.us/recording/abc123 (access shared with RapidRetail)

Next steps:
- Jordan will send the SLA addendum email with the proposed one-off credit by 2026-10-11.
- Karthik's team will open tracking tickets for A1/A4 and link to regression tests; updates every 48 hours until completion.
- Stephanie will host a weekly 30-min project sync until A2 and A1 are closed (first sync: 2026-10-14).

Anya — please reply to acknowledge acceptance of the timeline and owners or flag anything you want changed. We'll treat the EOD draft RCA as the baseline for the action tracker.

Thanks again for swift coordination — we take this seriously and will keep you updated.

— Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com

Attachments: rapidretail_rca_draft_v1.pdf, mitigation_runbook.xlsx
